rules.title: Newark municipal rent control / rent leveling ordinance (unverified)
rules.requirement: New Jersey has no statewide rent control, but municipalities may adopt rent control or rent leveling ordinances. Newark is believed to have one; check the Newark rent control ordinance and board for the allowed increase and covered units.
rules.citation: Newark Rent Control Ordinance (Newark Mun. Code)
rules.quoted_span: Municipalities may pass an ordinance establishing rent control or rent leveling.

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied small buildings or other local exemptions

rules.conflict_note: Unverified: the Newark code text (ecode360 link-only sources D070-D072) could not be read. Quoted span is from D067 (NJ DCA Truth in Renting), which says only that municipalities may adopt rent control; the 30-year new-construction exemption comes from N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5 as described in D067.
rules.review_note: Specific section, rates and exemptions of the Newark ordinance not verified.

no_rule_findings.finding: No Newark ordinance on algorithmic rent-setting appears in the documents. The NJ FAIR Act (P.L.2026, c.43, eff. 2027-07-01) governs statewide and bars municipal ordinances that conflict with it.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: A municipality shall be prohibited from enacting an ordinance that conflicts with this act.

parsed.notes: All provided documents are NJ state-level; they are not duplicated here. The Newark ecode360 sources (D070-D072) were link-only. Newark's rent control rule is added as an unverified low-confidence record. No Newark-specific just-cause, deposit, fee, screening or algorithmic ordinance was found in the readable documents.
